text:
Talorys

 Your personal AI agent. Your own cloud. 

Website: rociiu.github.io/talorys

Talorys is a free, open-source personal AI assistant that runs entirely inside
 your own Cloudflare account . It chats with you, remembers what matters,
manages tasks, notes and projects, and runs reminders and routines on a
schedule — without any server, database or account operated by the Talorys
developers.

One person. One Cloudflare account. One command. One personal AI agent.

 

Or install it with Appflare, which deploys it as a
single Worker:

 

---

 1. What Talorys is

- Today — a personal daily overview with your focus tasks, overdue and upcoming work, project activity, reminders and deterministic next-step suggestions. It is the first page you see, uses no AI, and links directly to the relevant task, project, automation or chat plan.
- A private assistant — chat with streaming responses, Markdown and tool activity indicators.
- Memory — durable personal facts and preferences you can view, edit and delete. Only the most relevant memories are sent to the model on each turn.
- Semantic recall (optional) — finds memories by meaning as well as keyword, lists them newest first with their saved date, and lets the agent find tasks, notes and automations by meaning. Off by default; turn it on with the Semantic memory recall switch near the bottom of Settings → AI (its other settings appear once it is on), or install with --semantic . See docs/semantic-recall.md.
- Memory history — facts that change over time: when you say you sold your car, Talorys asks you whether the old one is now a past fact, and with the optional AI check a confident answer does it for you. Unclear conflicts also wait for your review. See docs/memory-history.md.
- Tasks, notes and projects — full CRUD in the UI, and from chat ("Add a task to review my project tomorrow"). Project pages bring related work together with actionable task counts instead of estimated percentages. Chat task due dates reject impossible calendar dates, including timestamps with explicit UTC offsets.
- AI task planning — describe a goal ("Plan the tasks to launch my iOS app next month") and Talorys proposes a plan as an interactive card in chat. Review, edit or remove tasks, pick a project, then confirm: nothing is created until you do, and confirming creates everything at once, exactly once.
- Automations — one-time and recurring reminders, daily task digests and optional AI routines, delivered to an in-app notification center. They run on Durable Object alarms, so nothing has to stay online.
- Push notifications — reminders, digests and routines also arrive as system notifications on the phones and computers you turn them on for, even when Talorys is closed (Settings → General). Uses standard Web Push, encrypted end to end; on iPhone and iPad, add Talorys to the Home Screen first.
- Chat alerts — a system notification when a reply finishes or needs your approval while you're in another window (Settings → General, per device). Talorys must stay open, since closing it stops the reply.
- Remote MCP servers (optional) — connect remote MCP servers in Settings → Integrations (no auth, a bearer token, or OAuth sign-in) and choose which of their tools Talorys may use. Tools start off, and calls that may change something wait for your approval. Not used by scheduled routines. See docs/mcp.md.
- Web search (optional) — let Talorys look things up on the web in chat with Tavily or Exa, using your own API key (both have free monthly allowances). Off by default; by default each query waits for your approval. Only the query is sent, and Talorys never opens pages. See docs/web-search.md.
- Single-user by design — no signup, no accounts, no teams. The installer sets the owner password.
- Works without AI — Today, tasks, notes, memories and reminders keep working if Workers AI is unavailable or your free quota is used up.

 2. How it works

 

- The browser only ever talks to your .pages.dev site. /api/ requests run a
 Pages Function that forwards them over a service binding to the agent Worker.
- The agent Worker is deployed with workers dev: false and preview urls: false :
 it has no public URL .
- Authentication and authorization happen in the Worker, not the frontend.
- Chat responses stream as Server-Sent Events end-to-end.

More detail: docs/architecture.md.

 3. Cloudflare services used

 Service Used for Free plan 
 --- --- --- 
 Cloudflare Pages Frontend + Pages Function Yes 
 Cloudflare Workers Private API Worker Yes 
 Durable Objects (SQLite) All data, scheduling alarms Yes 
 Workers AI Chat model ( @cf/zai-org/glm-4.7-flash ) Yes, daily allocation 

Talorys does not provision R2, D1, KV, Vectorize, AI Search, Workflows or any
paid service.

 4. Deploy

 

The installer:

1. Checks Node.js (22+) and uses its bundled Wrangler CLI (any globally installed wrangler / cf is detected but not required).
2. Verifies your Cloudflare login, or opens Cloudflare's authorization page in your browser .
3. Lets you choose an account (if you have several) and an agent name.
4. Asks for an owner password (hidden input, strength-checked). It is hashed locally with PBKDF2-SHA256 and stored only as a Cloudflare secret.
5. Generates a 256-bit session secret, a Web Push key pair, and unique resource names ( talorys- -agent , talorys- -web ).
6. Deploys the private Worker (creating its SQLite Durable Object), stores secrets, creates and deploys the Pages project with the service binding.
7. Verifies the live deployment (frontend, auth endpoint, unauthenticated rejection, storage health) without running any AI inference.
8. Prints the real URL reported by Cloudflare.

It writes a talorys/ directory containing talorys.json (installation id,
account id, resource names, URL — no secrets ) and the deployable artifacts.
Keep it for updates.

 Interrupted? Run the same command

install.title: Deploy
install.html:
npx create-talorys@latest

The installer:

  1. Checks Node.js (22+) and uses its bundled Wrangler CLI (any globally installed wrangler/cf is detected but not required).
  2. Verifies your Cloudflare login, or opens Cloudflare's authorization page in your browser.
  3. Lets you choose an account (if you have several) and an agent name.
  4. Asks for an owner password (hidden input, strength-checked). It is hashed locally with PBKDF2-SHA256 and stored only as a Cloudflare secret.
  5. Generates a 256-bit session secret, a Web Push key pair, and unique resource names (talorys-<id>-agent, talorys-<id>-web).
  6. Deploys the private Worker (creating its SQLite Durable Object), stores secrets, creates and deploys the Pages project with the service binding.
  7. Verifies the live deployment (frontend, auth endpoint, unauthenticated rejection, storage health) without running any AI inference.
  8. Prints the real https://….pages.dev URL reported by Cloudflare.

It writes a talorys/ directory containing talorys.json (installation id, account id, resource names, URL — no secrets) and the deployable artifacts. Keep it for updates.

Interrupted? Run the same command again in the same place. It reconciles what already exists: no duplicate resources, no password re-prompt if the password is already configured, and no data is ever deleted.

Non-interactive installs: TALORYS_OWNER_PASSWORD=... npx create-talorys@latest --yes --account-id <id> (with CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN set if you are not logged in).

Permissions

Browser login uses Wrangler's standard OAuth flow — no Global API Key. If you use an API token instead, it needs:

  • Account › Workers Scripts › Edit
  • Account › Cloudflare Pages › Edit
  • Account › Workers AI › Read
  • Account › Account Settings › Read
  • User › User Details › Read (optional; shows your email)

See docs/deployment.md.
